lines: {player}: Nina! A girl came out of Willow Pond after the rumble. She says she's you. She's got freckles, orange hair and a stripy hat.
A me? From the pond? (Nina goes very quiet.)
Mum says the pond's deep. Deeper than ponds should be. I guess it goes somewhere else too. Like the portal.
She's not me. She's not a part of me, either. She's just another Nina, from another world. And I don't think she's a very nice one.
Go and find her at the pond. I'll be right here. Being... sensible. (She makes a face.)
She went back through the pond? Good. I think. Is it weird that I feel a bit sorry for her?
Everyone there must be sweet on the outside and tricky on the inside. That sounds tiring.
{player}! {player}! Look! It's SNOWING!
It never snows here. Not ever. Mum says it's been autumn in Stars Hollow for as long as anyone can remember.
(She catches a snowflake on her mitten and stares at it.) It's like something somewhere got unstuck.
We HAVE to build a snowman. It needs a carrot nose. Kip's got carrots at the Corner Market.
And Prue's got an old red scarf she never wears. It's by our door. Meet me on the green!
{player}! {player}! Feel that? The sun's actually HOT!
Mum says Stars Hollow's never had a proper summer. Not ever. It's like the whole year got its rhythm back.
(She's already wearing sunglasses. They're upside down.) We are having a BEACH DAY. At Willow Pond. Today.
Prue's got an old swim ring by our door, and Hank sells buckets and spades at the hardware store. Meet me by the dock!
{player}! Smell that? Rain AND flowers. Mum says Stars Hollow's never had a proper spring. Not ever.
But there was a big shower in the night, and Mother Duck's lost all five of her ducklings! She's on the bank of Willow Pond, quacking her head off.
They'll have waddled all over town. Find them and they'll follow you, ducklings follow ANYONE. Then we take them home. Go go go!
You turned the old stone dial by the oak, didn't you? I KNEW it. The whole town went whoosh!
Mr. Page says it's in his book. When a season comes home from wherever seasons go, the oak lets you pick it. Like a radio, but for weather!
Prue wants to turn it every five minutes. Mum said once a day. Prue said that's not what the dial said.
A carrot from the Corner Market, and Prue's scarf from our door. Then the green! Hurry, before it melts! (It won't melt. I just like saying it.)
You got them! OK. You roll the big ball, I'll do the head. Go on, start rolling! (It's just here by me.)
I left my sled on top of Lookout Hill. Go on, you first! I'll watch from the bottom and do the scores.
That was a ten. A ten! Now cocoa. Gus makes it with tiny marshmallows, but only if you ask nicely. Ask him!
Our snowman's still on the green. Prue visits him every morning. She's named him Sir Carrots.
Prue's swim ring from our door, and a bucket and spade from Hank's. Then the beach by the dock! Last one there's a soggy sandwich.
You got them! OK. You dig, I'll do the towers. The beach is just there, by the dock. Four towers. And a flag. Non-negotiable.
Best sandcastle EVER. Now: cannonball off the end of the dock! Run all the way to the end. I'll do the scores.
That was a ten. A TEN! I'm soaked. Lemonade time. Gus does pink lemonade in summer, but only if you ask nicely. Ask him!
Our sandcastle's still on the beach. Prue's put a crab in charge of it. Well, a pebble. She says it's a crab.
Five ducklings: by the gazebo, the playground, outside the bakery, the footbridge, and the Tulip Field. Walk right up to them. They'll follow you in a line!
Look at them all, in a line behind you! Take them to Mother Duck, on the bank by the dock. Don't walk too fast, their legs are THIS long.
They're home! Now the best bit of a spring shower: PUDDLES. There's three on the green. Jump in them. Properly. With both feet.
I'm wet up to my knees. Honey buns! Poppy makes them warm in spring. Ask her at the bakery, I'll be there!
The ducklings swim round the pond in a line behind their mum now. Prue's named them all. They're all called Gerald.
Oh! Hi. Good morning! You opened the door. I wasn't sure anyone lived here yet.
I'm Nina. Nina Blastoff. I live on Maple Lane, with my sister Prue and my little brother Bruno.
{player}: Hi Nina! I'm {player}.
{player}. Cool name. So... can I tell you something weird?
(She glances up at the sky for a second, then back at you.)
Have you ever had the feeling something's about to happen? Something big? No? Just me. Never mind!
First, go and meet everyone! Mr. Palmer's by the gazebo. He knows everything about this town. Probably more than he says.
Walk up to anyone and press {interact} to say hi. And {player_menu} opens your menu, with your quests and a map of town. {map} goes straight to the map.
Then come and find me by the gazebo. I want to show you something. (She's already walking off.)
Have you met Mr. Palmer yet? Gazebo. Middle of the green. Can't miss him. He waves a lot.
And say hi to a couple of the others. Theo and Mr. Page are on the bench by the gazebo. Ozzie tells a lot of jokes.
You've met everyone! Well, nearly. Now I want to show you something.
This is the notice board, right here by the gazebo. Go on, press {interact} on it. I'll tell you how it works.
Pick a job and follow it, and a star shows you where to go. You can follow two, or all three!
When it's done, come back to the board and press {interact} to turn it in. Sparkles!
(She grins.) That's how you get rich in Stars Hollow. Well. Sparkle-rich.
That was the BEST first day. I have to go home now, though. Mum's making spaghetti, and Bruno always eats mine.
Stars Hollow's pretty at night. Have a look round, then get some sleep!
(She stops, and looks up at the sky.) Huh. Did the stars just... flicker?
Never mind. See you tomorrow, {player}!
{player}! You're back! Did you... did you FALL too?
{player}: The ground cracked open right under me! And then I fell out of the SKY!
Me too! Right through my bedroom floor. Bruno grabbed my hand and down we went.
(She lowers her voice.) And all those little aliens hugging us. And everyone else staring like we were a thunderstorm.
And look, we both got watches. (She holds hers next to yours.) Tally kept saying we're 'chosen'. Chosen for WHAT?
Bruno didn't get one. He's being SO smug about it anyway.
Oh! And this morning there's a big crack in the ground in front of the old oak. It wasn't there yesterday. Mr. Palmer put a cone next to it.
I don't think last night was an accident, {player}. Something made it happen. Do you think it'll happen again?

choice.text: Only one way to find out!
lines: Midnight, then. Let's be ready this time. (She does a little twirl.)
Me too. Mostly. (She grins.) The Void's still there, I can feel it. Like a song stuck in my head.
Hey, {player}. I was thinking. You know the old oak, and the Shift, and the Void?
I could show you round properly. Like it was your first night all over again. Everyone, everything, start to finish.
Brilliant! First: go and say hi to Mr. Palmer by the gazebo. I'll explain the rest on the way.

choice.text: No thanks, I know my way.
lines: Fair enough! If you change your mind, it's in your quest log. Any time.
Oh. Hey. You're the new kid on the green. I'm Nina. Nina Blastoff.
{player}: Nina? But you look... different.
(She tugs her bow and gives you a long look.)
Different from what? ...Never mind. Don't answer that. Not here.
{player}! Isn't the Frost Fair the best? I've had four cups of cocoa. Maybe five.
Watch the lanterns at nine. Last year they all floated right over the old oak and... kind of shimmered. Green. Weird, right?
{player}! Isn't the Summer Fair the best? I've had four ice lollies. Maybe five. My tongue's every colour.
Watch the lanterns at ten. Last year they all floated right over the old oak and... kind of shimmered. Green. Weird, right?
{player}! Isn't the festival the best? I've had four caramel apples. Maybe five.
Watch the lanterns at nine. Last year they all floated right over the old oak and... kind of shimmered. Green. Weird, right?
{player}! Isn't the Spring Fair the best? I've had four strawberry tarts. Maybe five.
Watch the lanterns at nine. Last year they all floated right over the old oak and... kind of shimmered. Green. Weird, right?
Every year I think the tree can't be bigger than last year. Every year it is.
Make a wish when the star lights up. I always do. ...No, I'm not telling you what it is.
Mine's the red one with the black bow. Obviously.
If you run backwards up the hill it goes higher. If you trip, it also goes higher. Ask me how I know.
Firefly Night's my favourite. Real fireflies AND fake ones that go boom.
Bruno counts every single rocket. He loses count at about nine.
Happy Hallow's Eve! I'm a vampire. (She shows you her plastic fangs.) Bruno's a meatball. Don't ask.
Mr. Palmer gives the best treats, but you have to listen to a story about the old oak first. Worth it.
No school today! Mum's making pancakes. Bruno's already had four.
Saturdays and Sundays are the best. Nobody tells you what to learn. You just... find things out.
Gus does a grilled cheese on weekends that's shaped like a snowflake. Well. He says it is.
It's a grilled cheese with a bite out of it. But I like it.
Gus does a grilled cheese on weekends that's shaped like the sun. Well. He says it is.
It's a grilled cheese with chips sticking out round it. But I like it.
Gus does a grilled cheese on weekends that's shaped like a pumpkin. Well. He says it is.
It's a grilled cheese with a bite out of it. But I like it.
Gus does a grilled cheese on weekends that's shaped like a flower. Well. He says it is.
It's a grilled cheese with four bites out of it. But I like it.
Willow Pond goes all still when there's nobody about. Like it's listening.
I come here at weekends to think. Mostly about the oak. And about where the ripples go.
Otis has a telescope in the window. I'm saving up for it.
Then I can see what's really up there at midnight.
(Nina's looking at the old oak.) It hums louder near midnight. You've noticed too, haven't you? Thought so.
My room. Red and black. Prue says it's 'gloomy'. I say it's 'dramatic'.
Skating with Bruno. He's better than me. For now.
Breakfast. Prue's built a fort out of cereal boxes. Mum's pretending not to see.
